newsitem.title: USA: HCC Insurance to buy Avemco in stock swap.
newsitem.headline: HCC Insurance to buy Avemco in stock swap.

text.p: HCC Insurance Holdings Inc. said Friday it has signed a letter of intent to acquire Avemco Corp., which specialises in aviation insurance, in a stock swap valued at $230 million.
Under the agreement, Houston-based HCC said it will offer one share of its stock for each share of Avemco in a tax-free pooling of interests.
Avemco's stock surged $6 to $25.375, while HCC fell $1.125 to $27.50 on the New York Stock Exchange at midday.

HCC had about 35.8 million shares outstanding as of Dec. 31, compared with Avemco's 8.3 million. HCC said it will have about 44 million shares outstanding after the deal closes in June, subject to a definitive agreement and approval by regulators and shareholders of both companies.

Avemco, based in Frederick, Md., underwrites speciality insurance, mainly for small to medium-size aircraft operators. It had revenues of $125 million in 1996 and over 475 employees in 21 offices in 15 states.
Avemco's position in the U.S. aviation insurance market would complement HCC in the international aviation market, HCC Chairman Stephen Way said in a telephone interview.
"Avemco was not for sale," said Way. "We approached them. We felt there were some good synergies between us."
He also said that in light of recent softness in the property and casualty market, the acquisition will help HCC continue its growth rate of more than 20 percent annually.
He did not make a specific estimate for 1997.
After the acquisition, HCC will have a market capitalisation of $1.3 billion, Way said. The deal will not affect HCC's 1997 earnings and will boost its 1998 earnings, he said.
